`React.PureComponent` already decides when to render again by comparing the old and new props and state. If you write your own `shouldComponentUpdate`, it replaces that comparison, so extending `PureComponent` no longer does anything. Keep one of the two.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/no-redundant-should-component-update" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
class Price extends React.PureComponent {
  shouldComponentUpdate(nextProps) {
    return nextProps.amount !== this.props.amount;
  }

  render() {
    return <span>{this.props.amount}</span>;
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
class Price extends React.PureComponent {
  render() {
    return <span>{this.props.amount}</span>;
  }
}

class Total extends React.Component {
  shouldComponentUpdate(nextProps) {
    return nextProps.amount !== this.props.amount;
  }

  render() {
    return <strong>{this.props.amount}</strong>;
  }
}
```
